title: Nvidia is building an AI safety team, and it has a business reason
excerpt: Nvidia is quietly staffing an AI safety and security team as it doubles down on open-weight models. The logic: safer AI wins customers who need its chips.
content_html:
You can read Nvidia’s philosophy in a job advert. The chipmaker is assembling a new AI safety and security engineering team, Business Insider reported. A cluster of listings posted late last month gives it away. The pitch is not caution about what AI might do. It is a bet that trust is what makes people buy it.

The team is small but senior. Nvidia wants a distinguished engineer as its “founding technical leader”. It is also hiring a security research engineer, an evaluation engineer and a senior manager. Their brief, per the listings: vet AI agents before deployment, and build AI-powered tools that patch software flaws.

The case for open

One listing states the belief plainly. It calls open-weight models, transparency and broad scientific scrutiny “foundational to American AI leadership and cybersecurity defense”. Open-weight models publish the trained weights that decide how a model behaves. The training data and source code stay private. They are the opposite of the closed systems built by OpenAI and Anthropic.

Nvidia has been making this argument loudly. In his first ever post on X last month, chief executive Jensen Huang shared a letter urging US policymakers to back open models. They “strengthen safety and cybersecurity”, he wrote. Days later, Nvidia became a founding member of the Open Secure AI Alliance.

The 120-company group includes Microsoft, Palantir and SpaceX, and is building open-source security tools. The safety-team listings appeared just before that launch, and describe much of the same work.

Why safety sells chips

The philosophy has a balance sheet behind it. Open models put AI into far more hands than a closed service does. Every new user needs silicon to run it. That is why rivals such as AMD are chasing the same open-source opening. Nvidia does not want to cede it. More adoption means more chips.

Safety is the part that unlocks the adoption. AI is shifting from chatbots to agents that can reach sensitive company data and act on it. At that point the barrier stops being capability and becomes trust. A company will not hand an autonomous agent the keys to its systems unless it believes the thing is safe.

That is why firms now test agents for unauthorised actions before switching them on.

The open-model case is not settled. Critics argue that publishing weights hands capable tools to bad actors as readily as to defenders. Researchers have documented a safety gap, where open models match the frontier on capability but trail it on safeguards.

Nvidia did not respond to Business Insider’s request for comment, so its own account rests on the adverts. And it is worth noting who gains if the argument wins. The company insisting that safe, open AI should spread everywhere also sells the hardware it runs on.

content_html_zh:
你可以在招聘广告中读到 Nvidia 的理念。 据《商业内幕》报道，这家芯片制造商正在组建一个新的人工智能安全和安保工程团队。 上个月末发布的一系列列表暴露了这一点。 其宣传并不是对人工智能可能做什么的警告。 这是一个赌注，信任是人们购买它的原因。

团队虽小，但资深。 英伟达希望一位杰出的工程师作为其“创始技术领导者”。 它还正在招聘一名安全研究工程师、一名评估工程师和一名高级经理。 根据清单，他们的简介是：在部署之前审查人工智能代理，并构建人工智能驱动的工具来修补软件缺陷。

案件公开

一份清单清楚地表明了这一信念。 它将开放权重模型、透明度和广泛的科学审查称为“美国人工智能领导力和网络安全防御的基础”。 开放权重模型发布决定模型行为的经过训练的权重。 训练数据和源代码保持私密。 它们与 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 构建的封闭系统相反。

英伟达一直在大声疾呼这一论点。 上个月，首席执行官黄仁勋在 X 上发表的第一篇文章中分享了一封敦促美国政策制定者支持开放模式的信。 他写道，他们“加强了安全和网络安全”。 几天后，英伟达成为开放安全人工智能联盟的创始成员。

这个由 120 家公司组成的组织包括 Microsoft、Palantir 和 SpaceX，正在构建开源安全工具。 安全团队列表就在发布之前出现，并描述了大部分相同的工作。

为什么安全卖筹码

这一理念背后有一个资产负债表。 开放模型比封闭服务让更多人掌握人工智能。 每个新用户都需要芯片来运行它。 这就是为什么 AMD 等竞争对手也在追逐同样的开源开放。 英伟达不想放弃它。 更多的采用意味着更多的芯片。

安全是解锁采用的部分。 人工智能正在从聊天机器人转变为可以获取敏感公司数据并对其采取行动的代理。 到那时，障碍就不再是能力，而是信任。 除非公司相信该东西是安全的，否则公司不会将其系统的密钥交给自主代理。

这就是为什么公司现在在开启代理之前测试其是否有未经授权的行为。

开放模型案尚未解决。 批评者认为，出版权重既可以向不良行为者提供有用的工具，也可以向捍卫者提供有用的工具。 研究人员已经记录了一个安全差距，即开放模型在能力上与前沿相匹配，但在保障措施上落后于它。

英伟达没有回应《商业内幕》的置评请求，因此它自己的说法依赖于这些广告。 值得注意的是，如果争论获胜，谁会受益。 该公司坚持认为安全、开放的人工智能应该传播到世界各地，同时还销售其运行的硬件。
